title: The guard refuses `git checkout -B` or `switch -C` of a branch another worktree holds
why: Lane fix-check-after-notes-commit saw it twice on Nov 7 (record commit 9b2a11b9e, builder commit 391d4deea). Three worktrees held one branch through `git checkout -B <branch>`. A commit from one carried a stale index and undid another worktree's pushed work. The harm is a silent undo of pushed code.
note: Remedy line: `git checkout --detach origin/<branch>`, then `git push origin HEAD:<branch>`. Built by guard two-worktrees-one-branch, in lane session_013NEJKyzA8bkZSm147VHnke, which is in review round 2 and has reproduced this incident. That lane also covers `switch -C` (coordinator, 15:53 CST). Related steps: checkout-b-current-branch, agent-push-moves-held-branch and worktree-unique-branch. Done check: a red test on -B of a branch that another worktree holds. Sighting 10:05 CST Nov 8 (lane pr-review-range-check): two agent briefs both ran `checkout -B review-range-check` in separate worktrees; the test-author's push moved the branch under the builder's tree and left it stale. This is the step's own case.
